project.name: Climate Time Machine — NASA Global Climate Change

why: A first-party climate explainer keeps one spatial stage legible while readers switch scientific topics, scrub a bounded time range, and compare regional sea-level scenarios. It is a useful reference for pairing a temporal control with explicit context rather than treating animation as decoration.
dataShape: Climate observations and modeled scenarios organized by topic, time range, geographic region, and sea-level threshold.

hierarchy.evidence: The official interactive separates sea ice, carbon dioxide, global temperature, ice sheets, and sea level into distinct climate stories.
Readers scrub topic-specific annual ranges; the sea-level story also selects regional projections across one- to six-meter thresholds.

encodings.mapping: A geographic field is paired with sequential color and a visible time control so the reader can connect change to a selected period.
A selected location and threshold expose the consequence of a scenario without changing the surrounding explanatory frame.

interactions.evidence: The official entry point lets readers choose a climate indicator before entering its dedicated time-based visualization.
Each topic presents a defined observation range and a draggable temporal control rather than an unbounded animation.
The sea-level experience changes regional context through explicit one- to six-meter options.

accessibility.evidence: When adapting this pattern, expose the active topic, year, location, and scenario as text-labelled controls so a temporal or color change is not the sole carrier of meaning.
Retain a concise textual interpretation for the selected state and do not make comprehension depend on animated map imagery.

capture.attribution: NASA Global Climate Change; visualization credits and underlying scientific sources are identified within the NASA Climate Time Machine experience, including NASA Scientific Visualization Studio for the feature.
capture.reusePolicy: inspiration-only — distill topic switching, bounded timeline, and scenario-selection patterns in an original preview. Do not copy NASA imagery, maps, data labels, logos, or identifiers; NASA media guidance requires acknowledgement and individual third-party materials may have separate restrictions.
